assessment: This 60-card pool is three piles. First, spares: Agent of Treachery, Chasm Skulker, United Front, Stroke of Genius, White Sun's Zenith and five lands (Adarkar Wastes, Flooded Strand, Glacial Fortress, Hallowed Fountain, Prairie Stream) duplicate maindeck cards and cannot legally enter while their copy remains — they are printing variants, not options — and the remaining lands sub-pool (Temple of the False God, Radiant Fountain, taplands) never beats the current 33-land base given 50 blue pips and measured land-drop decay. Second, a fair-value blue draw pile (Vision Skeins, Trade Secrets, Pull from Tomorrow, Homesickness, the creature cantrips) that is strictly worse than the engines already in the 99. Third — the part that matters — about a dozen on-plan cards forming three coherent packages: turn-protection (Grand Abolisher, Drannith Magistrate) that directly hardens the verified 002 Approach window and the 004 loop turn; a draw-payoff/mill constellation (Teferi Temporal Pilgrim, Teferi's Tutelage, Jace Beleren, Jace Wielder of Mysteries riding the maindeck X-draw suite) that gives the deck its first win axes needing neither combat nor the punisher two-piece; and one trap package — Walking Ballista / Hangarback Walker / Inspiring Statuary as 004-loop payoffs — which the loop's verified mana-neutral ledger refutes (X=0 forever, and improvise never applies to the loop's artifact casts). The pool contains zero punisher-half cards, so it cannot directly close the 34.3% two-piece consistency gap; what it honestly offers is engine-half redundancy (Jace Beleren) plus alternate lines that make the 65.7% of games without the two-piece winnable anyway.

swaps.when: Any pod holding instant-speed interaction — which at this deck's bracket-4 floor is every pod; cast it the turn you commit to the second Approach or the Hullbreaker loop, not before.
swaps.why: Stack 002's only loss window is opponents' instants on the second Approach cast; Abolisher's text — opponents can't cast spells or activate artifact/creature/enchantment abilities during your turn — closes that window for two mana, while Greaves only gives haste and shroud to a 4/4 the deck rarely needs to attack with.

citations.quote: The window opens when your win attempt either can't be profitably answered — protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for

swaps.when: Pods where commanders are recast twice-plus a game or anything casts from exile or graveyard (cascade, flashback, Breach-style) — i.e., most bracket-4 tables; bench it only in the rare all-from-hand pod.
swaps.why: Opponents can't cast from anywhere but their hands: it strands every commander this deck bounces with Hullbreaker Horror or Cyclonic Rift in the command zone, while United Front is the worst of the deck's three X token spells — sorcery-speed Allies with no Ally or go-wide payoff, in a list whose verified wins are all noncombat.

swaps.when: The midgame stall where you sit on draw engines waiting for a punisher — and any meta with sweepers, where Skulker's death payoff is cleaned up in the same wrath that kills it.
swaps.why: Both are draw payoffs, but under Teferi's Ageless Insight plus the Mine effects Pilgrim gains 3-5 loyalty a turn — arriving turn 5 and climbing out of burn range immediately — and the -2 token grows on every draw, while Chasm Skulker only pays off by dying, which this deck never wants to let happen.

swaps.when: When you want a win that needs neither combat nor the 34.3% two-piece — best in removal-light, counter-heavy pods where a resolved walker sticks and the maindeck X-draw suite is live.
swaps.why: White Sun's Zenith's {W}{W}{W} is the heaviest colored cost in a deck with 11 white land sources and its Cats are an off-plan combat wincon; Jace is a standalone draw engine whose static turns the maindeck's own Stroke of Genius or Braingeyser, self-targeted for X ≥ library under Heliod's discount, into a win (line flagged in opens_lines, needs a stack scenario).

citations.quote: unsynergistic win conditions dilute the list

swaps.when: Whenever two-piece assembly is the complaint — the swap adds a table-draw engine copy that keeps triggering after land drops dry up, which per goldfish is turn 5 onward in about half of games.
swaps.why: Horn of Greed's trigger decays with the measured land-drop rate (57.1% at t5, 48.4% at t6) exactly when the engine must be online, while Beleren's +2 draws each player every single turn — feeding Iron Maiden hands and Heliod's discount unconditionally — and his -10 folds into the Tutelage mill axis.

citations.quote: consistency has two purchases: redundancy (more cards doing the job) or tutoring (cards that fetch it)

swaps.when: Attrition pods without graveyard decks — mill feeds Breach- and recursion-style tables, so bench it against those; sleeve it wherever games go long and the punisher half is missing.
swaps.why: It is the second copy of the maindeck Sphinx's Tutelage effect: with Teferi's Ageless Insight doubling your draws the pair converts a normal turn cycle into 8-16 mill, a second inevitability axis for the 65.7% of games without the two-piece; Brass Infiniscope is a four-mana rock that cannot join the 004 loop (recasts mana-negative at {4} for {C}{C}) and only cantrips when an X-spell follows it.

citations.quote: the linear deck needs redundancy that shrugs off three answers

opens_lines.why_plausible: Jace's static replaces the empty-library draw with a win; the maindeck X-draw suite self-targeted for X ≥ library size presents exactly that draw, and Heliod, the Warped Eclipse's per-opponent-draw discount (huge on Forced Fruition turns) plus Folio of Fancies/Reliquary Tower/Thought Vessel no-max-hand insurance make the X affordable and the hand legal. Laboratory Maniac is the redundant second copy of the win clause. Unverified: the X arithmetic, the mid-resolution replacement timing, and what happens if Jace leaves the battlefield partway through the draws.

002's framing is that the second cast's only window is the stack; Abolisher forbids opponents casting spells during your turn, which would close that window entirely — but Abolisher restricts only spell casts and artifact/creature/enchantment activations, so channel lands (an opponent's Otawara bouncing Abolisher itself from their hand) and planeswalker/land activations remain legal on your turn. Whether the window is truly shut, and against exactly what, needs a walkthrough.

Fraying Sanity counts cards put into the enchanted player's graveyard from anywhere this turn, and this deck forces cleanup-step discards from Fruition-bloated hands (stack 003's trim-to-7 subtlety) — but Fraying Sanity triggers at the beginning of the end step, before cleanup discards happen, so whether trimmed cards ever count (including via a second cleanup round under CR 514.3) is a genuine open rules question that decides whether the curse doubles the punisher engine or misses it entirely.

A free Approach via Omniscience is still cast from hand, which the win condition requires, and the deck's table-draw density plus Heliod's generic discount can realistically pay {7}{U}{U}{U}; free countermagic from hand then defends the second cast. Unverified: the cast-from-hand satisfaction under alternative costs, the timing of the win check, and the honest cost of note — every X-spell in the deck resolves at X=0 when cast for free.

long_term_defaults.why: Every verified win this deck has (002 second Approach, 004 loop, the 003 punisher board deployed ahead of interaction) is committed on its own turn, and two mana protects all of them; there is no pod at this bracket where you would rather hold Lightning Greaves.

Commander recasts and non-hand casts appear in essentially every bracket-4 game, and it compounds the deck's own bounce plan by stranding rebought commanders in the command zone — live unconditionally, not situationally.

In a deck drawing 3-5 cards a turn under its own engines the loyalty snowball makes him effectively unkillable in combat while the -2 token grows per draw; the strictly better use of the draw-payoff slot Chasm Skulker holds.

A fine standalone draw engine at {1}{U}{U}{U} on a 36-blue-source base, plus the deck's first wincon that rides the X-draw suite instead of combat or the 34.3% two-piece — worth the slot even before the self-draw line is verified.

The only true engine-half redundancy in the entire 60: a repeatable each-player draw for three mana that keeps feeding punishers and Heliod's discount after land drops fail, where Horn of Greed goes quiet.
Second copy of the Sphinx's Tutelage effect in a deck that draws in multiples every turn — effect-class redundancy for the mill axis that carries games where the punisher half never shows.
Redundant copy of Jace's win clause on a 2/2 that dies to any removal mid-draw; sleeve it only if the self-draw line verifies and the pod is light on creature removal — never ahead of Jace.
Good card, wrong queue: it competes with Temporal Pilgrim for the walker slot and gains far less from the deck's draw density; first alternate if a slot opens.

Reads like the dream and is actually a trap: reducing each opponent's maximum hand size by seven makes them trim toward zero at cleanup, so they arrive at their punished upkeep with empty hands — it switches OFF Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke and Viseling, the deck's verified 003 clock, to play a different deck's game.

The tempting 004-loop outlet fails on the verified ledger: the loop is exactly mana-neutral (3 in, 3 out per cycle), so Ballista only ever recasts at X=0, enters as a 0/0, and dies to SBAs into the graveyard — it cannot rejoin the loop and deals zero; with the two-card infinite refuted (001) there is no infinite mana anywhere to sink.
Same arithmetic as Walking Ballista: the mana-neutral loop caps X at 0, and a zero-counter Hangarback dies leaving zero Thopters.

Improvise applies only to nonartifact spells — the 004 loop casts Sol Ring and Arcane Signet, both artifact spells, so Statuary never touches the loop's ledger; and outside the loop, tapping a rock for improvise yields the same {1} its mana ability would. It converts nothing here.

The Approach package is real if a scenario verifies it, but nine mana with no built-in protection is the one-spectacular-finisher shape that loses to a single answer, and every X-spell in the deck is dead (X=0) when cast for free under it.
Worth a slot only if the cleanup-discard timing question in opens_lines resolves favourably; on its face it deepens mill on one opponent while this deck's engines mill all three shallowly.
Its static makes the second Approach uncounterable — real tech for counterspell wars — but it is seven mana for protection Grand Abolisher gives at two on the only turn that matters.

Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount on a Forced Fruition turn can shave double-digit generic off the cost and the deck can flash it in — a genuine haymaker, but off-plan, and the arithmetic is uncomputed: goldfish explicitly does not model cost reducers.

Same discount logic as Emrakul with a weaker payoff for this deck: nothing here makes opponents sacrifice, so its second ability is nearly blank and Annihilator is a combat plan the deck doesn't have.

Backup fuel for the Jace line and an instant-speed punisher push, but maindeck Stroke of Genius already fills the slot, and BSZ's shuffle-back clause complicates the empty-library math — same scenario would need to cover it.
Without shuffle density (the 99 offers Flooded Strand, Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans) it rearranges more than it draws; every engine card it could displace does more.
All three modes play and {U}{U}{U} is fine on a 36-source blue base, but the maindeck counter suite is already seven deep at better rates; first replacement if the suite thins.
Fine rate, but the existing suite is deeper and cheaper; the exile clause is its one edge — sleeve it against recursion pods specifically.

Banned in Commander (cards.csv legal_commander: 'banned') — it can never enter the 99, so it is a dead slot in the pool regardless of its text; even were it legal, the opponent controls the repeats and stops precisely when it would profit you.
Its five-lands condition is live in barely half of games by the measured land-drop rates (57.1% at t5), and Ancient Tomb already serves the colorless-burst job without ever being a dead draw.
Colorless-only in a deck with 50 blue pips across 34 spells; two life does not pay for the {U} it can't produce.
Sorcery-only flash when the commander's back face and Leyline of Anticipation grant broader flash already, and the Ring text is blank in a deck with no tempt sources.
Her upkeep draw needs a creature to have entered last turn and goldfish shows a mean of 1.4 bodies deployed by turn 6 — the trigger misses more turns than it hits.

The X=10 mode shuffles your graveyard back into your library — direct anti-synergy with the Jace/Lab Man empty-library line this same pool proposes — and as a plain X-draw the maindeck already runs five.

gaps: Trade Secrets' legality is settled, not open: cards.csv marks it banned in Commander, so it is excluded from every swap and line above — recorded here because sideboard-facts and bracket_report (maindeck-scoped) did not surface the flag.

The strategy corpus has no section on group-slug donation risk (already noted in strategic_frame.gaps), so the evaluation of Vision Skeins, Trade Secrets and Homesickness rests on card reading alone rather than a citable principle.

The pool contains zero punisher-half effects, so no swap can directly raise the 34.3% two-piece-by-t6 rate; a goldfish re-run after the Jace Beleren swap would quantify what engine-half redundancy actually buys, but goldfish does not model cost reducers or the swap set, so that number is currently uncomputable.

Four candidate lines need resolve-stack runs before any is played as fact: the Jace/X-draw self-deck win, the Grand Abolisher window closure (channel-land loophole included), the Fraying Sanity cleanup-discard timing, and the Omniscience free second Approach.

Emrakul/It That Betrays castability under Heliod's discount is arithmetic no current artifact computes — goldfish's stated assumptions exclude cost reduction — so their 'live earlier than the curve suggests' claim is oracle-text reasoning only.
